previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and gastrostomy dependence due to intractable nausea, was admitted for severe nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea lasting 24 hours. He was found to have acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, with improvement after intravenous fluids. Stool studies were negative for infectious pathogens, supporting a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis, possibly norovirus. His chronic diarrhea was managed by restarting opium tincture after clearance. He tolerated oral intake by discharge, with creatinine improving to 1.7. His immunosuppressive regimen was continued without complication. He was discharged home with services on a stable medication regimen, including new prescription for ondansetron for nausea, and instructions to resume G-tube feeds and maintain hydration.
